description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral fire extinguisher asset identity, configuration, ownership, and lifecycle control record for a portable fire-protection unit whose location, accessibility, charge, condition, maintenance status, and hazard suitability must remain traceable. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.label: Record reference and timing
Facility, location, and responsible parties

blocks.guidance: This Fire Extinguisher record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: Unit is in its designated place and its asset tag matches the location record
Access, visibility, mounting, cabinet, and directional marking are documented
Operating instructions and hazard rating are legible and face outward
Pressure indicator or charge condition is recorded without assuming serviceability
Pin, tamper seal, handle, hose, nozzle, horn, and discharge path are observed
Cylinder, cartridge, shell, base, and threads show no visible damage or corrosion
Leakage, agent loss, prior discharge, fire exposure, and contamination are recorded
Inspection tag, annual maintenance date, and supporting service record are linked
Hydrostatic-test and internal-maintenance dates are routed for qualified verification
Agent class and rating are checked against the documented hazard and occupancy plan
Recall, replacement, recharge, and out-of-service status are reconciled
Alternate protection is documented whenever the unit is removed from service

blocks.guidance: A checked item confirms the control was addressed; it does not substitute for the referenced procedure, permit, test, or source.
items: Physical nameplate and location are distinguished from imported inventory data
Asset ID, parent system, child components, served area, and owner are mapped
Capacity, rating, configuration, utilities, controls, and interfaces are recorded
Manuals, drawings, warranties, permits, certificates, and commissioning records are linked
Maintenance plan, service history, failure history, spares, and vendor route are visible
Criticality, redundancy, outage impact, replacement lead time, and contingency are assessed
Changes preserve prior values, effective date, source, approver, and superseded record
Retirement, transfer, disposal, data retention, and downstream inventory changes are controlled

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Extinguisher is missing, discharged, depressurized, leaking, or visibly damaged
Cylinder has corrosion, pitting, heat exposure, mechanical injury, or suspect repair
Pin, seal, hose, nozzle, horn, valve, handle, or pressure indication is compromised
Access is obstructed or the unit cannot be safely reached and identified
Agent class, rating, mounting, or location may not match the documented hazard
Maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic test, recall, or condemnation status is unresolved
A unit is removed without documented alternate protection and facility notification
Inspection evidence conflicts with the tag, inventory, service label, or provider record

blocks.guidance: Do not resolve a checked stop condition by inference, an unchecked box, or a generic sign-off. Preserve the condition, protective action, authority, evidence, owner, due point, and verified disposition.

blocks.label: Asset Register decision, timing, and authority

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: Physical identity and source documents support the current register values
Configuration, location, parent-child, utility, and control relationships reconcile
Criticality and contingency reflect current service and redundancy
Warranties, permits, certificates, inspections, and service requirements have owners
Record changes identify source, approver, effective date, and prior value
Retirement or transfer includes physical, financial, environmental, and data disposition
Qualified fire-protection provider reviews recharge, repair, testing, and condemnation work
Location and hazard suitability are confirmed against the approved fire-protection plan
Removed or rejected equipment has replacement or alternate-protection evidence
No inspection mark is treated as proof of internal condition or future performance
Service dates, tags, seals, and inventory status reconcile before acceptance
Facility owner approves any temporary gap, restriction, or follow-up due point

blocks.guidance: Do not use this Fire Extinguisher record as permission for work outside the approved scope, as proof that an unperformed test passed, or as a substitute for required qualified-person, employer, authority, or manufacturer approval.
blocks.label: Decision-use limitation

sections.guidance: Separate the authorized decision from preliminary observation and record its limits.
sections.title: Fire Extinguisher qualified decision and authorization

blocks.label: Asset Register outcome and primary handoff

blocks.guidance: Unchecked items require an exception disposition or a documented reopen trigger before the record can be treated as closed.
items: Accepted unit is mounted, visible, accessible, sealed, and identified in its assigned place
Rejected unit is tagged, segregated, and routed for qualified service or disposal
Replacement or alternate protection is installed and communicated when required
Inspection, maintenance, recharge, and test records are linked to the exact serial or tag
Inventory and protected-area records reflect the final location and service state
Open deficiency, responsible owner, due point, and verification method are recorded
